correctness.rationale: For a nonempty complement, restrained domination is exactly the conjunction that each omitted vertex has a selected neighbor and an omitted neighbor. Nested chain neighborhoods reduce these two requirements to a nonempty-proper prefix condition on the B-side at the minimum omitted A-class and a nonempty-proper suffix condition on the A-side at the maximum omitted B-class. Necessity follows from vertices in those two extremal classes; sufficiency follows by neighborhood nesting. The three relative orders of the extremal indices exhaust the counting cases and give the stated factors without overlap. Direct exhaustive verification agrees with both the characterization and coefficient formula on 687,124 subsets of 540 canonical chain-graph profiles through order 11.

value.rationale: The chain-graph minimum restrained domination problem is already solved, so another formula for minimum restrained domination number alone would be routine. The accepted result instead classifies every restrained dominating set through a unique extremal boundary pair and yields every polynomial coefficient, the total number of restrained dominating sets, the number of minimum sets, and minimum restrained domination number in one O(p^2) enumerator. This is a structural extension of a specifically studied graph class and a named polynomial invariant, not an arbitrary finite slice or table recomputation.
